title: Support bundle tradeoffs and cost hypotheses for private deployments
body:
Purpose:
This working note captures hypotheses and lightweight sensitivity calculations around how we should structure licensing + support bundles for private deployments (on-prem and VPC) to maximize customer adoption while protecting unit economics. Not a final financial model — companion spreadsheets live in the /sheets folder (see linked artifacts).

Quick summary / recommendation hypothesis (top of doc):
- Offer three core bundles (Core, Managed, Enterprise). Core is low-touch license + self-install support; Managed adds remote ops + 24/7 incident response; Enterprise bundles include on-site support / professional services and a multi-year SLA option.
- Price anchors: Core should be positioned as ~30–40% discount vs equivalent hosted per-month token bill at steady state for customers who commit to 12 months; Managed should price to recover ~40–65% of ops cost under realistic utilization bands; Enterprise targets >100% recovery of eng + PS time for high-touch customers.
- Primary lever: migrating a portion of customers from ad-hoc professional services into Managed subscription reduces PSA churn and improves LTV/LTV:CAC quickly.

Audience and context:
- Audience: Product leadership, pricing, GTM, and Solutions Engineering.
- Context: We are seeing increasing inbound interest for on-prem deployments from regulated customers but friction on initial procurement due to unclear support delineation and perceived cost variability. This doc argues for clearer bundle definitions and headroom allowances for hardware variance.

Definitions and base assumptions used for quick math (base-case month):
- Reference customer: midsize SaaS company, 3 production services, expected steady-state qps equivalent = 250 tokens/s across serving fleet.
- On-prem hardware: 4x A100-80GB equiv nodes; list price amortized capex per-node = $80k; install / racking / networking one-time = $25k.
- VPC deployment: reservation equivalent cost (cloud committed discount) = $20k/mo for comparable capacity (including GPU hours + networking).
- Software license: per-node perpetual license amortized monthly (base-case) = $2,500/node/mo (on-prem).
- Support labor cost: senior SRE blended fully loaded = $220k/year (~$18.3k/mo).
- Managed ops roster: 1 FTE supports ~6 similar customers for Managed bundle at steady state.
- Professional services (PS) one-time onboarding average = $35k (50% time for on-prem network/ops).
- Amortization horizon: 36 months for capex by default.

Mini-table (simplified monthly view, numbers rounded):
- On-prem base monthly (amortized):
  - HW amortized: (4 * $80k) / 36 = $8,888/mo
  - Install/rack amortized: $25k / 36 = $694/mo
  - License: 4 * $2,500 = $10,000/mo
  - Ops (internal) incremental: assume 0.25 FTE = $4,575/mo
  - Total on-prem monthly baseline = ~$24,157/mo

- VPC base monthly (reservation):
  - Cloud reservation: $20,000/mo
  - License (hosted variant): included in reservation (we model price parity by adjusting feature deltas)
  - Ops delta (cloud-managed): 0.05 FTE = $915/mo
  - Total VPC monthly baseline = ~$20,915/mo

Observations from base-case: on-prem has modest premium driven by license + hardware amortization and incremental ops. The gap is ~15% on the numbers above, but PS onboarding spikes create customer reluctance and procurement negotiations.

Sensitivity axes to prioritize in spreadsheet and in sales motions: (we should run 3x3 grids for these)
1) Utilization variance (60% / 80% / 95% of assumed token throughput) — affects effective cost per unit of work and amortization coverage.
2) Time-to-deploy / PS effort (low/medium/high) — if PS >$70k the on-prem value prop can break without Managed+PS bundled discount.
3) Support FTE efficiency (FTE per customer for Managed) — 1:4, 1:6, 1:10 scenarios.
4) Hardware price movement (±20%) and cloud reservation pricing (±25%).

Hypothesis-driven pricing mechanics we want to test in spreadsheets:
- Core bundle: flat license + limited support (response SLA = 48 hours), PS sold separately. Price target: license-only yields ~20–35% margin on average contract across 36 months (expect sticker friction for customers).
- Managed bundle: license + Ops hours + remote incident management + monthly health checks. Price target should recover ~50–70% of expected ops cost (rest subsidized to hit adoption). Include a variable surcharge tied to peak token-hours above committed baseline.
- Enterprise bundle: managed + guaranteed SLOs, on-site quarterly checks, white-glove onboarding included. Price target aims to fully recover expected PS + a 20% margin. Offer term discounts for 24/36-month commitments.

Examples of bundle math (rounded, per month):
- Core: license-only = $10k (license) + $1k (support retainer optional) = $11k/mo.
- Managed: license + ops = $10k + $3,500 = $13.5k/mo (assuming 1/6 FTE allocation).
- Enterprise: license + ops + PS amortized = $10k + $7,000 + $1,200 = $18.2k/mo (PS amortized and on-site costs).

Break-even and churn levers (qualitative):
- Move customers into Managed by packaging onboarding discounts (waive 50% of PS fees if commit to 12-month Managed). This shifts one-time PS spend into recurring revenue and reduces churn risk.
- Allow hardware substitution credits: certify a set of 3 hardware partners with pre-negotiated discounts and include a hardware procurement concierge as part of Enterprise bundle. This reduces procurement negotiation cycles.
- Introduce an "Auto-scale burst" add-on priced at a premium for customers who need occasional peak capacity. This monetizes peak events and limits overprovisioning.

Checklist for spreadsheet runs (what I will send to analytics):
- Build 36-month cashflow for each bundle (Core/Managed/Enterprise) for on-prem and VPC variants.
- Model 4 customer archetypes (startup, midsize, enterprise-regulated, enterprise-scale).
- Sweep utilization (60/80/95), PS spend (20/50/200% of base), and FTE efficiency (1:4, 1:6, 1:10).
- Output: NPV (discount 10% annually), payback months, gross margin, ARR retention sensitivity.

Open questions / unresolved tradeoffs (items for discussion):
- Should we allow per-node perpetual license transferability between on-prem fleets owned by the same customer? This affects upsell math and secondary market concerns.
- Discounting policy: what’s the guardrail for offering deeper discounts to Enterprise in exchange for longer terms vs guaranteed capacity?
- PS packaging: should we push more PS into a distinct SOW (and keep Managed cleaner) or bake a standard onboarding into Managed?

Immediate next steps and owners: (quick execution plan)
- Marcus Li: author and finalize the scenario spreadsheet template and run baseline runs (due 2025-01-31).
- Jenna Marquez: coordinate Solutions Eng to tag three live prospects for model validation and gather PS actuals (due 2025-01-20).
- Owen Brooks: draft contractual language options for license transferability and managed SLAs (due 2025-02-05).
- Priya Sharma: liaise with finance to align discounting guardrails and target gross margin bands (due 2025-01-28).

Notes to reviewers (quick):
- This is intentionally math-light; the spreadsheet will contain the heavy lifting. Looking for alignment on bundle definitions and which sensitivity axes to prioritize.
- If we agree, I will create a short slide deck for GTM (3 slides) showing recommended bundle structure and 2–3 pricing anchors for sales enablement.

Raw scratch / quick scenarios (copied from an adhoc calc session):
- If PS average = $70k and we convert PS into a 12-month Managed subscription at $6k/mo extra, payback period for the added Managed fee is ~11–12 months and average churn risk reduces materially.
- If hardware prices drop 20% (for customers using spot-pricing or used hardware), on-prem edge over VPC flips favorable for price-sensitive customers; propose a lower-tier Core-Lite license for that cohort.

Appendix: suggested sheet tabs (spreadsheet to build)
- Summary dashboard (NPV, payback, margin)
- Assumptions tab (editable knobs)
- Per-customer 36mo cashflows (detailed)
- Sensitivity matrix outputs (heatmaps)
- PS and SOW ledger (actuals by project)
summary: Working hypotheses and sensitivity checklist for structuring licensing + support bundles for private deployments (on-prem vs VPC). Draft outlines recommended bundle tiers, base assumptions, example math, sensitivity axes, and execution next steps.
